pkgmetadata.longdescription:
A fork of i3lock-color adding the opt-in --fido2-or-password option, which starts FIDO2 authentication alongside the normal password prompt so that whichever succeeds first unlocks the screen. An absent or failed key does not count as a password failure, and password authentication stays available throughout.
The FIDO2 path requires a separate PAM service named i3lock-fido2, which this package deliberately does not install: a package must not silently add an authentication path to the system. An example is installed as documentation. Without that service, --fido2-or-password fails closed and password authentication behaves exactly as in upstream i3lock-color.
This fork is intended to be temporary and exists while the feature is proposed upstream. Upstream i3lock-color is packaged in ::guru as x11-misc/i3lock-color; this package blocks it because both install /usr/bin/i3lock.
